statement: Wallachia maintained a complex relationship with the Kingdom of Hungary as a nominal vassal that frequently asserted effective independence. Hungarian kings claimed suzerainty over Wallachia as a buffer against Tatar and later Ottoman pressure; Wallachian voivodes paid tribute and provided military service intermittently. The Battle of Posada (1330) — in which Wallachian Prince Basarab I defeated Charles I of Hungary's invasion force in a mountain ambush — established Wallachian de facto independence. Mircea the Elder maintained a more cooperative relationship with Hungary as a counterbalance to Ottoman pressure, but never accepted permanent Hungarian control.
